messages:
raj_cust_inc: We're getting intermittent 504s when calling the Redwood API after moving to the interface endpoint. Only happens from our corp network (Zscaler/TLS-inspect proxy in front).
ana_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share a short repro (curl) and any TLS logs you have?
raj_cust_inc: Minimal repro: from a laptop inside corp. curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```
* curl -v output *
*   Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.10.10.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed, cipher=...
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```
raj_cust_inc: Note: the IP returned by DNS is 10.10.10.5 (our corp proxy). When I curl from a bastion in the same VPC I get the endpoint private IP and 200.
ana_support: Okay that points to split-horizon/DNS or proxy rewriting. Can you paste a dig +short and an openssl s_client snippet?
raj_cust_inc: dig +short api.redwood.example.com -> 10.10.10.5
```
* openssl s_client -connect 10.10.10.5:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -brief *
* Certificate chain: CN=corp-proxy-int, issuer=Corp-CA
```
raj_cust_inc: So the proxy is terminating TLS and presenting our internal cert.
mike_infra: If the proxy terminates TLS, it will re-open a separate connection to the endpoint. That backend leg might be timing out or hitting an allowlist block. Two quick checks: 1) does the proxy allow direct connect to the VPC ENI IPs? 2) are ephemeral ports/NACL allowing the return traffic?
lisa_sre: Also confirm the VPC endpoint's security group allows 443 from the proxy SG or its public egress IPs.
ana_support: Can you try an explicit override to test? From your laptop:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```
(Replace 10.0.5.12 with the interface endpoint ENI IP you see from the VPC bastion)
raj_cust_inc: Ran that — got HTTP 200. So direct to the ENI works.
ana_support: That confirms DNS/proxy path is the issue. Two remediation paths:
- Fix corporate DNS so api.redwood.example.com resolves to the VPC endpoint IP within your corp network (split-horizon) OR configure conditional forward to Route53 private hosted zone that points to the endpoint.
- If you must go via the TLS-inspect proxy, add an egress rule so the proxy bypasses TLS inspection / performs passthrough for api.redwood.example.com, or add an allowlist for the proxy to connect to the endpoint ENI IPs and ephemeral ports.
mike_infra: One more gotcha: if the proxy rewrites SNI or performs MITM, Redwood's backend may see incoming Host/SNI not matching cert, and our routing rules may drop the request or return 504 if backend times out. If you can't bypass inspection, we recommend SIPH (split-brain) DNS.
raj_cust_inc: How do we map Route53 private zone into our DNS? We don't own the account where the endpoint is.
lisa_sre: two options: 1) Have the VPC endpoint owner create a private hosted zone and share it with your account (Route53 resolver rules / inbound endpoints) or 2) create a conditional forwarder in your DNS to resolve that name using the endpoint owner's VPC DNS resolver IPs.
ana_support: Also please confirm endpoint state: run this from the service owner's account/bastion:
```
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters "Name=service-name,Values=com.amazonaws.vpce.service-*-redwood" --query "VpcEndpoints[*].[VpcEndpointId,State,PrivateDnsEnabled,NetworkInterfaceIds]" --output table
```
raj_cust_inc: I pasted output from them earlier — state=available, PrivateDnsEnabled=true, interfaces in subnets A/B.
mike_infra: Check the endpoint SG allows inbound 443 from your proxy's egress SG or proxy IP range. Also check any NACLs on the endpoint subnets that might block ephemeral ports (1024-65535).
raj_cust_inc: NACL was blocking ephemeral on one subnet — we just opened it.
ana_support: Nice. After that change, can you test again without --resolve?
raj_cust_inc: Testing now... got 200 consistently from a couple clients. Looks stable. Thanks.
ana_support: Great. TL:DR of recommended steps we gave you:
- Prefer split-horizon / conditional DNS forwarding so endpoint IPs are resolved directly inside corp.
- If using TLS inspection, configure proxy bypass or allowlist for endpoint IPs + ephemeral port range, and preserve SNI/Host.
- Ensure endpoint SGs and NACLs allow proxy egress IPs and ephemeral ports.
- If endpoint lives in another account, set up Route53 sharing or resolver inbound rules.
raj_cust_inc: Filing this with our infra team to update DNS and NACLs. Thanks for quick help :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: VPC endpoint acceptance event: vpce-0abc123 accepted by service-owner-account at 2024-10-12T15:12:33Z :white_check_mark:
lisa_sre: If you want, we can run a short synthetic check from Redwood's side to confirm back-end logs show successful connections; ping me once you've flipped the DNS so we can verify.
raj_cust_inc: Will do. Thanks all.
